title: Scott Joplin's playing and piano rolls
summary: Carew relays opinions of Joplin's playing and they discuss rolls labeled as Joplin.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Never recorded, no. Well, now I heard something different from that, to the truth, there's something that... late... No, no, no, no. A fellow from Indiana, Joe Russell Robinson. He commented on a tune that, St. Thomas Spencer's tunes that was played to some singer. He said, if you're listening to hear Williams play on that, he didn't, or he couldn't. He said, I'm the man that played to come in for that. That was Russell Roberts. I don't know anything further than that. It's Spencer Williams. Spencer, yeah. Spencer Williams. So I don't know. You hear lots of tales about it. They say that Joplin wasn't a very good player. He's not, not compared to the other boys. But I heard a party that lived in Memphis, I think it was Memphis, that told me that if they could get Scott Joplin for their parties to do the play, they didn't want anything else. He offered that remark off hand.
Well, don't you think this is probably Joplin on these roles that like this... I'm pretty sure they do. I mean, the label says just one thing. It says the title in Scott Joplin, and that's all.
I have a pretty strong feeling also I've heard of that role by the Maple Leaf. I think he played that too. I heard that.
It sure sounds like, I don't know who else it could be who would play that way, you know.
Well, he follows the music group much on this than the gladioles. That's what he's making at all. No, that's just what I wish.
